advice: A short gap in your CV shouldn't be an issue, especially before a master's degree.
quote: I have interviewed at 18 companies (which wouldn't have been possible if I was still working) and of course everyone asked about this break, I told them the truth that I wanted to take some time off from work and that's it.
author: farkas

situation: The author worked in the corporate world and found the hiring process illogical and incompetent.
choice: They quit their corporate job and returned to graduate school.
outcome: They found academia to be highly competent, with graders reading papers and grades matching knowledge.
main_reason: They preferred the competence and fairness of academia over the illogical corporate environment.
advice: Go to the interview, get the job, gain experience, then leave for a better environment.
quote: Years later, I have quit corporate work and returned to graduate school. I am still amazed at the high levels of competence in academia
author: Astor Florida

situation: Author discovered that former difficult colleagues were at the company where they had a job interview.
choice: Declined the new job offer after realizing the role differed from expectations and involved the former colleagues.
outcome: The author sent a message declining the position and bid farewell to the company.
main_reason: The job description was too different from what was expected and involved working with disliked colleagues.
advice: The author did not provide advice to others in the post.
quote: Anyway, I just sent an inMail stating that the job described was too different than expected, thanked them for their time and bid them farewell.
author: Jaeger

situation: they were in a PhD program with insufficient funding
choice: they submitted their PhD thesis as a Master's thesis and switched to another PhD program with a better stipend
outcome: they finished the PhD, completed two postdocs, and became a tenured full professor
main_reason: funding issues at the original university
advice: switching universities because of funding is a cleaner reason than advisor or labmate problems
quote: I had no problems gettting postdocs (2) and I'm now a tenured full professor.
author: Cheery

situation: they were dealing with a problematic supervisor and felt the situation was unfair
choice: they quit their Ph.D. program to reapply in a different field
outcome: they are now in the fourth year of the new Ph.D. program
main_reason: the supervisor was problematic and the environment was stressful
advice: they should first try contacting the supervisor, then consider changing supervisors, departments, or leaving the Ph.D. altogether
quote: I quit to reapply a Ph.D. program in a different field (also my major in undergrad) and currently 4th year in the new program.
author: user22080

situation: they were a graduate student in a lab with an abusive, unethical PI at an R1 university
choice: they gave an ultimatum and left the lab, moving to another professor’s lab
outcome: they left the toxic lab; the former PI later lost students and faced no formal repercussions
main_reason: the PI was tyrannical, emotionally abusive, and unethical
advice: leave quietly and frame the move as a mismatch with your interests
quote: Two years later she had no students, and was finding it hard to recruit.
author: bfoste01
